subject: ClearSimple capacity pathway checklist & GPU sizing follow-up
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@clearsimple.ai>, Sasha Li <sasha.li@clearsimple.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: ClearSimple post-demo: capacity checklist and next steps

Alex / Sasha — great to meet today, quick recap and the data we need to finalize a Dedicated sizing recommendation. Attaching the workbook we referenced.

Key takeaways from the call (high level):
- Customer preference: Dedicated pool for production (data isolation + predictable throughput) but evaluating a short-term Hosted fall-back for burst traffic.
- Primary workload: multi-turn chat + JSON-structured tool calls; occasional batch reranking.
- Performance needs: P95 generation latency target ~300ms for the 95th percentile, soft P99 < 800ms.

What we need from you to size the pool precisely (please send by next Tue):
1) TPS targets: expected sustained token-generation TPS (tokens/sec) across business hours and expected peak TPS during marketing events. If you track requests/sec instead, include average tokens/request (separate prompt and completion).
2) Token mix: distribution of input vs output token lengths (median, 75p, 95p). Example: median prompt 40 tokens, median completion 120 tokens.
3) Concurrency profile: typical concurrent sessions and how long sessions remain warm (KV cache reuse).
4) Percent of requests that require tool-calls or larger multimodel routings (e.g., initial embedding + generation).
5) Compliance constraints: do you need Private VPC / on-prem (yes/no)? If so, which timeline for audit/approvals?

Initial sizing notes (rough, from call):
- If you target 25k tokens/sec sustained with 300ms p95 and a token mix of ~30% input / 70% output, we typically recommend H100 80GB nodes for best latency headroom and quantization flexibility; A100 80GB is also viable at slightly higher latency and better throughput per dollar in some workloads. For mostly short responses (<64 tokens), L4-style GPUs can be cost-effective but will struggle on longer multi-turn KV cache workloads.
- Autoscaling/burst: we recommend a base reserved pool sized for sustained load + a burst buffer for 2x spikes during promotions.
- Fallback: we can route non-latency-critical jobs to Hosted or lower-cost GPU variants when Dedicated pool saturates.

Next steps (proposal):
- You: populate the attached capacity workbook with the fields above. Include one week of request traces if possible (anonymized).
- Us: we’ll return 2 size options (latency-optimized and cost-optimized) with estimated RU consumption and monthly committed pricing.
- POC: after sizing, propose a 2-week Dedicated pilot with defined traffic mirroring and SLA check-ins.

Attachments: clearsimple_capacity_workbook_v2.xlsx (workbook template), redwood_dedicated_pricing_v1.pdf (pricing bands)

Thanks — EV

Evelyn Hart
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@clearsimple.ai>

Cc: Sasha Li <sasha.li@clearsimple.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 16:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ClearSimple post-demo: capacity checklist and next steps

Thanks Evelyn — useful summary. Quick answers and a couple follow-ups:  

- We’ll fill the workbook by Monday EOD.
- Quick numbers from our observability: typical business-hour traffic ~120 reqs/sec. Average tokens/request currently ~220 (prompt 50 / completion 170). Peak during launch day saw ~520 reqs/sec for ~20 minutes.
- Concurrency: sessions tend to be long (clients keep sessions open ~6–8 minutes) and we see good KV reuse for ~80% of traffic.
- Multi-model: ~18% of requests also hit retrieval/embedding flow before generation.
- Private VPC: not required for initial rollout — will evaluate for Q4. We do need SOC2 evidence and audit logs.

Question: given our peak patterns, would you recommend H100 to meet the P95 300ms target, or can A100 pools plus aggressive batching hit it? Concerned about cost during sustained 120 reqs/sec baseline.

Alex
Alex Morgan
CTO, ClearSimple
alex.morgan@clearsimple.ai
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: ClearSimple post-demo: capacity checklist and next steps

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Alex’s quick numbers. Can you:  

1) Run a short capacity estimate comparing two configurations for ClearSimple baseline (120 req/s sustained, avg 220 tokens/req, peak 520 req/s bursts):
   - Option A (latency-first): H100 80GB nodes, N cores, assume minimal batching to hold p95 <= 300ms for the median token mix; include KV cache reuse assumptions (80% warm).
   - Option B (cost-first): A100 80GB nodes with more aggressive batching and burst buffer; target p95 ~350–450ms and p99 <900ms.
2) Provide RU/tokens estimates and monthly committed pricing (use the pricing bands in the attached pdf). Include a simple sensitivity table (if peak doubles, recommended burst capacity).
3) Note implications for multi-model routing (18% retrieval/embedding traffic): recommend whether to colocate embedding model on same pool or route to separate L4-style cheaper nodes.

Put the output into the shared drive link and we’ll push back a short slide for Alex. Also note any quantization concerns for their multi-turn KV reuse (we should recommend mixed precision / 4-bit when safe).

Thanks — EV

Evelyn / team — thanks for the quick turnaround. We’re happy to proceed with the pilot once you confirm a recommended baseline. Next immediate step: can we lock a POC kickoff for the week of 6/28? We’ll have product and infra on the call; legal wants an SOW draft ahead of the kickoff (simple pilot SOW + acceptance criteria).

I’ve uploaded the partial workbook to the Drive link you shared (clearsimple_capacity_workbook_v2.xlsx) — the traffic sheet has sample logs for Mon–Fri last week. Expect the completed workbook Monday.

For SOW: include a clause for data retention (30 days logs), SOC2 evidence scope, and a rollback/fallback plan to Hosted API if Dedicated pool experiences a hard outage. Also confirm whether you can provide a 24/7 on-call during the pilot window (our infra team may need that for initial cutover).

If you can confirm 6/28 kickoff and a SOW draft by 6/24, we’ll be ready.

Best,
Alex
